article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Bubblegum Runtz × Zamosa #29
Breeder: LA Family Farms
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: 0.1–0.14%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , humulene, beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Orange candy, sweet citrus, tangerine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8-9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Medium

Orange Drip arrived with something many modern cannabis strains chase but relatively few achieve: a flavor identity strong enough to become the plant’s calling card. Developed by L.A. Family Farms from Bubblegum Runtz and the selected Zamosa #29, the hybrid leans heavily into bright citrus candy rather than the simple lemon or orange-peel character associated with older citrus weed. Its reputation grew rapidly in California’s connoisseur scene, and Orange Drip earned unusually strong recognition at the 2026 California Zalympix, where L.A. Family Farms took Industry awards for Best Tasting and Best Terps. The cultivar also placed first in People’s Choice for Best Overall, Best Terps and Best Tasting.

That performance helps explain why Orange Drip is better understood as a terpene-focused premium hybrid than simply another high-THC marijuana strain. Current commercial flower has tested around 26% THC with very little CBD, placing potency comfortably in the upper range of today’s recreational cannabis market. Its appeal, however, comes from the combination of potency, resin production and an orange-candy profile that remains noticeable from the initial aroma through the finish.
Genetics and Lineage

The documented genetics are Bubblegum Runtz × Zamosa #29, with L.A. Family Farms credited as the breeder and selector. Genetics catalogs carrying the breeder cut identify the same parentage and specifically preserve the Zamosa parent as the #29 selection. That distinction matters because numbered selections represent a particular phenotype rather than every plant that might be grown under the Zamosa name. Orange Drip therefore reflects a deliberate pairing rather than simply a generic combination of two strain families.

Bubblegum Runtz contributes the modern candy side of the equation, while Zamosa #29 pushes the cross toward sharper fruit and citrus character. The result is distinctly contemporary California cannabis: sweet enough to fit within the candy-genetics category but carrying enough spice, gas and depth to prevent the aroma from becoming one-dimensional. Instead of burying its citrus beneath heavy fuel, the plant keeps orange near the front of the profile.

Its competition results provide additional evidence that the selection was made with aroma and flavor in mind. Winning both terpene and taste categories is particularly notable because THC percentage alone cannot create those traits. The prominence of Orange Drip in sensory judging suggests that the breeder successfully stabilized a recognizable aromatic expression in the selected commercial cut.
Effects and Experience

Orange Drip delivers the type of experience expected from potent modern hybrid marijuana, but its progression is generally more buoyant than narcotic. The beginning can feel quick and cerebral, bringing greater sensory intensity, an elevated mood and a lively mental quality. Conversation, music, gaming and other recreational activities may feel more engaging during this early period. With THC hovering around the mid-20% range in documented flower, inexperienced consumers should approach the cultivar conservatively rather than assuming its bright flavor corresponds with mild potency.

As the experience develops, the initial lift tends to settle into a calmer hybrid state without necessarily producing the heavy physical shutdown associated with strongly sedating weed. That balance gives the cultivar broad appeal for afternoon or evening use when relaxation is desirable but complete inactivity is not. Higher doses can naturally change that equation, producing stronger mental haziness and heavier physical relaxation.

Tolerance, consumption method and individual cannabinoid sensitivity remain important. Someone accustomed to high-THC cannabis may experience Orange Drip as manageable and social, while an occasional consumer could find the same flower considerably more intense. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness or anxious overstimulation are possible with excessive THC consumption.
Medical Benefits

Orange Drip has no strain-specific clinical trials establishing it as a treatment for any medical condition, so medical claims should remain conservative. Its combination of substantial THC and an uplifting-to-relaxing experience may nevertheless appeal to some medical marijuana patients seeking temporary relief from stress, low mood or difficulty unwinding. Others may find that THC’s effects on appetite and sensory perception make food more appealing when poor appetite is an issue.

The terpene composition also deserves attention without overstating its significance. Commercial listings have identified myrcene, humulene and beta-caryophyllene among important aromatic compounds in Orange Drip flower. Terpenes are biologically active molecules, but the presence of a particular terpene does not demonstrate that smoking or vaporizing this cultivar will treat inflammation, pain, anxiety or another medical disorder.

Patients taking prescription medications, people sensitive to THC and anyone using cannabis for a diagnosed condition should therefore treat Orange Drip as cannabis rather than a standardized pharmaceutical product. Cannabinoid and terpene concentrations can change between harvests, meaning the response to one batch may not precisely predict another.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The first impression is unmistakably citrus-forward, but calling Orange Drip simply “orange flavored” misses much of its character. The aroma resembles sweet orange candy, tangerine syrup and freshly opened citrus sweets, followed by a warmer layer of spice and faint gas. Breaking apart the flower can reveal more of the peppery and earthy underside, producing a contrast between bright fruit on top and darker cannabis notes underneath.

Interestingly, available retail terpene information has listed myrcene, humulene and beta-caryophyllene among its key compounds rather than automatically assigning limonene as the dominant terpene simply because the weed smells citrusy. This is a useful reminder that cannabis aroma results from numerous volatile compounds working together; a strain’s flavor cannot always be predicted from one dominant terpene.

During consumption, the sweeter elements tend to arrive first. Orange candy and ripe citrus give way to mild pepper, herbal warmth and a restrained gassy finish. That layering helps separate Orange Drip from older Tangie-style cultivars whose sharp citrus can dominate virtually everything else.
Growing Information

Reliable cultivation specifications for Orange Drip remain limited. The authentic cultivar circulates as an L.A. Family Farms breeder cut, and available genetics documentation specifically avoids assigning fixed flowering days or yield figures without controlled cultivation data. For that reason, claims that the plant universally finishes in a particular number of weeks or produces a specific grams-per-square-meter yield should be treated cautiously unless they can be traced to the breeder or a documented grow.

Commercial examples demonstrate that the cultivar is capable of producing premium indoor flower with strong resin and desirable bag appeal. Growers working with a verified cut should record stretch, internodal spacing, branch strength, flower density and maturation timing during the first cycle rather than designing an entire room around undocumented expectations.

Because preserving aroma is one of the main reasons to grow this cultivar, environmental stability becomes especially important late in flowering and during drying. Excess heat, poor humidity control and overly aggressive drying can diminish the volatile compounds responsible for the orange-candy character. Careful curing is equally important if the goal is flower resembling the terpene-rich examples that established Orange Drip’s reputation.
FAQ
Is Orange Drip an indica or sativa?

Orange Drip is best classified as a hybrid. L.A. Family Farms has not established a meaningful indica-to-sativa percentage that should be treated as authoritative, so assigning a precise ratio would be speculative.
What are the genetics of Orange Drip?
The verified lineage is Bubblegum Runtz × Zamosa #29. L.A. Family Farms is credited with creating and selecting the cultivar.
How strong is Orange Drip?

Commercial flower has been listed at approximately 26.14% THC with around 0.14% CBD, placing it firmly within the high-potency category. Testing varies from harvest to harvest, so the package laboratory results should always take priority over a strain-wide number.
What does Orange Drip taste like?

Its defining profile combines sweet orange candy and tangerine with softer pepper, herbal and gassy notes. The flavor tends to remain citrus-heavy while offering more depth than a straightforward orange-dominant marijuana cultivar.
Who bred Orange Drip?

Orange Drip is associated with L.A. Family Farms, the Los Angeles cannabis producer responsible for the Bubblegum Runtz × Zamosa #29 selection. The strain became particularly notable after its multiple wins for flavor, terpenes and overall quality at the 2026 California Zalympix.
Final Thoughts on Orange Drip

Orange Drip represents the direction premium cannabis breeding has increasingly taken: distinctive flavor first, strong potency second and enough visual and resin quality to complete the package. Bubblegum Runtz supplies a modern candy foundation while Zamosa #29 gives the cross the vivid citrus signature that defines its identity. Instead of relying solely on THC numbers to attract attention, this cultivar earned recognition through aroma and taste, including multiple top placements in competitive judging.

For consumers who enjoy sweet citrus weed but want something more layered than traditional orange genetics, Orange Drip offers an especially interesting profile. Its mixture of candy, tangerine, spice and restrained gas gives it recognizable character, while the high THC content keeps the experience firmly within premium contemporary marijuana territory. Just as importantly for a reference guide, its documented lineage is clear while its cultivation specifications remain relatively private—making accuracy more valuable than filling those gaps with unsupported grow-room folklore.
